text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, each of the ten activities A33, A34, A35, A37, A38, A39, A40, A41, A42 and A43 ran in essentially every case (participation 1.0, about one occurrence per case). In the later window, A33, A34, A35, A37 and A38 each run in 92–95 of 200 cases and A39–A43 each in 109–111 of 200 cases, still about once per case in which they run. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010]
- These ten activities form two five-activity blocks that used to run one after the other and now exclude each other. Earlier, a first-block activity (A33/A34/A35/A37/A38) and a second-block activity (A39–A43) co-occurred in 100 in 100 cases, with the first-block activity first in about 97–99 in 100; in the later window such pairs co-occur in only about 1–3 in 100 cases, while in about 45 in 100 only the first-block activity runs and in about 53–54 in 100 only the second-block activity runs. This holds for all 25 observed cross-block pairs. [REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL033, REL034, REL035, REL036, REL037, REL040, REL041, REL042, REL043, REL044, REL046, REL047, REL048, REL049, REL050, REL051, REL052, REL053, REL054, REL055]
- Within each block the activities still travel together: first-block pairs co-occur in about 46 in 100 later cases (about 52–54 in 100 contain neither), second-block pairs in about 55 in 100 (neither in about 44–45 in 100), whereas every such pair co-occurred in 100 in 100 cases earlier; the order inside a block stays mixed in both windows. [REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL030, REL031, REL032, REL038, REL039, REL045, REL056, REL057, REL058, REL059, REL060, REL061, REL061, REL063, REL064, REL065]
- A30 and A31 still occur in every case in both windows and keep their roles: A30 precedes whichever block runs (e.g., A30 before A33 in about 46 in 100 later cases versus 99 in 100 earlier; A30 before A41 in about 54 in 100 versus 98 in 100), and A31 follows it (e.g., A33 before A31 in about 45 in 100 later cases; A42 before A31 in about 55 in 100). [REL001, REL003, REL006, REL008, REL011, REL016, REL019]
- Routing matches this: earlier, A30's observed outgoing transitions went almost only to the first block (A33–A38 at about 17–23% each); in the later window they split between the second block (A39–A43 at about 8–13% each, together about 53%) and the first block (together about 44%). A33, A34 and A38 now lead directly to A31 in about 21–25% of their observed outgoing transitions; earlier, A31 was not among their observed successors. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- Event positions (relative ranks, not clock time) shift consistently with a shorter middle segment: A30's mean position moves from about 0.55 to 0.64, first-block activities from about 0.62 to 0.72–0.73, second-block activities from about 0.75 to about 0.72. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010]
- Five-step lag support moves in step: A30→A41/A42/A43 pairs appear within five steps in 105–106 of 200 later cases versus 1–2 earlier; cross-block pairs such as A33→A41 fall from about 107–125 of 200 to 1–3; first-block→A31 pairs such as A33→A31 rise from 1–2 to about 88 of 200. The lag distributions on the 1–3-observation side are too sparse to describe the new spacings. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG013]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the segment between A30 and A31, which earlier ran in every case as two consecutive blocks (A30, then A33/A34/A35/A37/A38 in varying order, then A39/A40/A41/A42/A43, then A31), works in the later window as an either/or choice: about 46–48 in 100 cases run the first block, about 55 in 100 run the second block, and only about 1–3 in 100 contain both — that is, each block is now skipped in roughly half the cases. [OCC001, OCC006, REL025, REL027, REL040, REL051]

The change is shown directly by the relations between the activities, not only by marginal frequencies: cross-block pairs flipped from always co-occurring to almost never, while within-block cohesion and the A30-before/A31-after relations are preserved, and the routing evidence shows the bypasses that make this possible (A30 directly into the second block, first-block activities directly to A31). With 112 qualifying items against about 1.28 expected if nothing had changed, chance sampling cannot account for the pattern as a whole. [REL021, REL060, REL001, REL011, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, screening]

Limitations: the evidence does not show what decides which block a case takes, so a change in the mix of cases between the windows (rather than in the routing itself) cannot be ruled out from this control-flow evidence; the sparse lag distributions and the few remaining joint occurrences are not described in detail. [LAG005, LAG006]

Other differences: in the later window, A33, A34 and A38 each show a few additional weak outgoing transitions (about 1% of their observed outgoing transitions each) to activities outside the two blocks, such as A08, A13, A24 and A45, which were not observed earlier. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
